Optimization: your own track switch time at each station

Finds trips faster than the official planner shows. The planner only offers a change that takes at least the official track switch time, e.g. 5\u00A0min at Luzern. If you\'re quicker, an earlier train may still be yours.

The minutes in a box: from one train to the next, walk included. Set your own per station under Optimization (− and +). Otherwise: the official time minus the offset in Settings (⚙), e.g. 5\u00A0−\u00A01\u00A0=\u00A04\u00A0min at Luzern.

Green ↓: below the official time, orange: the same, red ↑: above. Official: the timetable\'s, or less where the planner itself changes faster. Red !: a delay leaves less than your time, grey: the next train is gone.
How much faster than the official trip, first departure to last arrival: 33 instead of 47\u00A0min is 42% (47\u00A0/\u00A033\u00A0=\u00A01.42).
A normal ticket covers the faster trip too, a supersaver ticket only the official train. A trip passing a station twice may need another ticket.

Delays (+3) and changed tracks as known at the search, only a few hours ahead; cancelled trains not. Whether you make it is up to you. The last result stays, also offline: check its day and how old its delays are.
Connections: transport.opendata.ch. Official track switch times: opentransportdata.swiss, timetable 2026. Not affiliated with SBB.
